title: Deadlock build code (decoded JSON)
description: The JSON shape of a decoded Deadlock build code. A build code is base64(zstd(protobuf)); decoding it yields the object described here. This is the machine-readable companion of marklock/organized/mechanics/build-codes.md, which is the canonical prose reference. The field names and the protobuf field numbers are those of decode_build_code.py and encode_build_code.py, mirrored by codec-site/lib/deadlock_codec.rb; the API shape of the same payload is BuildHero in deadlock-api/api-1.json (its mod_categories[].mods entries are objects with ability_id, while the local codec decodes them to a flat list of item ids).

hero_id.description: Hero the build is for. Protobuf field 1. Resolve with list_heroes or heroes_raw.json; validate_build.py raises an error for an unknown hero id.

version.description: Edit counter of the build. Protobuf field 2. The local client files use 13; published builds use 90-94.

hero_build_id.description: Id of this build. Protobuf field 3. In the client's own files it equals the local Steam account id; in published builds it is the per-hero build number.

author_account_id.description: Steam account that owns the build. Protobuf field 4.

name.description: Build title. Protobuf field 5. validate_build.py warns when it is empty.

language.description: Language of the build. Protobuf field 7. 0 (English) in every observed sample; no other value was ever seen.

origin_build_id.description: Id of the build this one was copied from. Protobuf field 8.

field_9.description: Protobuf field 9. Meaning unknown; copied through untouched and never set by this repository.

tags.description: Protobuf field 11, repeated varint. Holds the ability and upgrade ids the build references (a published Seven build carries 539192269, 2061574352, 1074714947).

field_13.description: Protobuf field 13. Meaning unknown in build codes; in the client's own cache it repeats the last-updated timestamp.

details.description: Protobuf field 10 of the build. Holds the item categories and the ability timeline.

mod_categories.description: Protobuf field 1, repeated. The item categories in the order the player wrote them.

ability_order.description: Protobuf field 2. Null when the build carries no ability order.

mod_category.description: One item category, the unit the client shows as a build panel box.

mods.description: Protobuf field 1, repeated message. The local codec decodes each entry to the item id only (its field 1); the live game also stores an annotation, a sell priority and an imbue target ability per entry, which the local codec drops.

name.description: Protobuf field 2. The category label. A free-form label: the client stores, renders and re-imports whatever text the author typed. The labels the client itself ships are the localisation keys #Citadel_HeroBuilds_Early, _Mid, _Late, _EarlyGame, _MidGame, _LateGame and _Lane, plus the plain phase names early, early-mid, mid, mid-late, late, late-late, optional spirit-resist and optional general-resist-sustain.

description.description: Protobuf field 3. Optional note shown under the label.

height.description: Protobuf field 4, float32. Cosmetic box height in pixels; not a fixed value and not required by the client.

width.description: Protobuf field 5, float32. Cosmetic box width in pixels; not a fixed value and not required by the client.

optional.description: Protobuf field 6, varint flag. Marks the category as optional in the client.

ability_order.description: The ability timeline: one entry per spend, in the order the player made it.

currency_changes.description: Protobuf field 1, repeated message. A fully maxed hero has 16 entries: 4 unlocks and 12 point spends (4 x -1, 4 x -2, 4 x -5).

currency_change.description: One spend in the ability timeline.

ability_id.description: Protobuf field 1. Ability id (type: ability in items_raw.json / list_items), not an item id.

currency_type.description: Protobuf field 2. 1 = ability points, 2 = ability unlock. validate_build.py errors on any other value.

delta.description: Protobuf field 3. Amount spent, always negative. The ladder the client writes is -1 for an unlock (currency_type 2), then -1, -2 and -5 for the three upgrade tiers (currency_type 1). validate_build.py errors on 0 and on positive values.

annotation.description: Protobuf field 4. Optional label shown in the client, for example '3rd skill'.

x-wire-format.evidence: decode_build_code.py (zstd magic check), codec-site/lib/deadlock_codec.rb (ZSTD_MAGIC), build.bin vs build.zst headers

x-categories.evidence: decode_kv3.py --builds on the client's cached_hero_builds.kv3 (94 distinct names, 79 of them player-authored); validate_build.py VALID_CATEGORIES

pairs.meaning: unlock one ability (one Ability Unlock each)

x-ability-order-ladder.spend_order: tier by tier or per ability; both shapes occur in the client's own saved builds
x-ability-order-ladder.evidence: decode_kv3.py --builds on cached_hero_builds.kv3 (439 entries: 2/-1 118, 1/-1 112, 1/-2 110, 1/-5 99); 40 published builds from https://api.deadlock-api.com/v1/builds?limit=40 (160 of each pair); mechanics/ability-points.md

x-id-resolution.item_ids: list_items (deadlock-api MCP) or items_raw.json, type: upgrade
x-id-resolution.ability_ids: list_items (deadlock-api MCP) or items_raw.json, type: ability
x-id-resolution.rule: Never invent an id. Item ids change with patches, so the lookup is the procedure, not a stored table.

x-verification.import_bar: decode the produced code back, run validate_build.py on it with 0 errors, and resolve every item and ability id against the game's own data

x-claims.claim: A build code is base64(zstd(protobuf)); a raw uncompressed protobuf payload is accepted too
x-claims.evidence: decode_build_code.py zstd magic check; codec-site/lib/deadlock_codec.rb ZSTD_MAGIC; build.bin vs build.zst headers; published codes from /v1/builds

x-claims.claim: The top-level keys map to protobuf fields 1-13 as listed in this schema
x-claims.evidence: decode_build_code.py get_int/get_str; encode_build_code.py encode_field; codec-site/lib/deadlock_codec.rb build_hash and encode_top

x-claims.claim: A mod_category uses fields 1-6 (mods, name, description, height, width, optional) and a mods entry holds the item id in its field 1
x-claims.evidence: decode_build_code.py mod_categories parsing; encode_build_code.py encode_category; deadlock_codec.rb parse_category; BuildHeroDetailsCategory in deadlock-api/api-1.json

x-claims.claim: A category name is a free-form label; the client ships 7 #Citadel_HeroBuilds_* keys and 8 plain phase names, and imports names outside the validator's set
x-claims.evidence: decode_kv3.py --builds on the client's cached_hero_builds.kv3 (94 distinct names, 79 player-authored); validate_build.py VALID_CATEGORIES (warning only)

x-claims.claim: An ability order carries 4 unlocks (currency_type 2, delta -1) plus 4 x -1, 4 x -2 and 4 x -5 point spends (currency_type 1)
x-claims.evidence: decode_kv3.py --builds on cached_hero_builds.kv3; 40 published builds from /v1/builds; the 43 generated builds in codec-site/test/fixtures/files/builds_all_heroes.md

x-claims.claim: currency_type must be 1 or 2 and delta must be a negative integer
mods entries hold item ids while ability_order entries hold ability ids
x-claims.evidence: items_raw.json resolves every id in build.bin to an item of type upgrade; the ability ids of Seven resolve to type ability

x-claims.claim: height and width are cosmetic and not fixed
x-claims.evidence: 171 distinct (height, width) pairs across 40 published builds; the client's own files use 861.75 x 172.5, 807.0 x 205.5 and 840.75 x 192.0

x-claims.claim: The payload in the client's cached_hero_builds.kv3 numbers the hero id in field 2, while this schema (following decode_build_code.py) labels field 1 hero_id and field 2 version
x-claims.evidence: marklock/organized/mechanics/hero-build-cache.md: 23 of 24 builds with an ability order carry only their own hero's ability ids; Haze - Oracle Build has field 1 6 and field 2 13
